_doc: Module 6 quiz · 3 scenario items, each a different decision from the practice steps: a row that answers a question about ownership (q1), a product question that needs no row (q2) and a GDPR follow-up that goes past its row (q3). Every item is open-job-aid: the learner sees the job aid while answering, because the assessment tests use of the aid, not recall (Rossett & Schafer, 2007).

items.stem: Sven says the company belongs to three members of his family and asks how much work signup will be for them. What do you do?

options.label: Read the AML row, because these checks are about financial crime
options.rationale: The AML row is about checking payments once the account is open. The checks before an account opens are on the KYC row.

options.label: Book the compliance team, because ownership questions go to them
options.rationale: The KYC row sends ownership thresholds and lists of documents to compliance. Sven only asked how much work signup is, and the row's line answers that.

options.label: Read the KYC row
options.rationale: Checks at signup are what the KYC row covers. Its line already says that the owner needs about 10 minutes and that everyone with a large stake goes through the same check.

options.label: Tell him that only the person who signs the contract has to be checked
options.rationale: That is a guess, and the job aid says the opposite: everyone with a large stake goes through the check.

items.stem: Tom, the founder of a SaaS company, asks "Does it tag software subscriptions and travel as separate expense categories?" Which row do you use?

options.label: The GDPR row, because expense records hold personal data
options.rationale: Expense records do hold personal data, but Tom is asking what the product does with categories, and the GDPR line says nothing about that.

options.label: Book the compliance team, in case it touches accounting rules
options.rationale: Compliance can't tell him how the product tags spending. A regulatory answer to a product question sounds as though you are dodging it.

options.label: The PSD2 row, because these are card payments
options.rationale: The PSD2 line is about the licence you work under and says nothing about expense categories.

options.label: No row, because this is a product question
options.rationale: Expense categories are a product feature. Answer it as you would any product question, or note it for the demo.

items.stem: A buyer follows up on GDPR and asks how fast you answer a data request from a Swiss former employee who wants their full card history, and which transfer mechanism covers Switzerland. What do you do?

options.label: Message the compliance team and book a follow-up with the buyer
options.rationale: Deadlines for data requests and transfers outside the UK and the EU are on the GDPR row's escalation list. Book the follow-up while you are still on the call.

options.label: Read the GDPR row, since it covers where data goes
options.rationale: The GDPR line says where data is stored and who it is shared with. It gives no deadline and no rule for Switzerland.

options.label: Say that Switzerland has an adequacy decision, so transfers are covered
options.rationale: That is an answer on a legal point from memory. If any part of it is wrong, the buyer's lawyer will find it.

options.label: Say the deadline is one month, and check the transfer question after the call
options.rationale: The deadline depends on which law applies to the request, and that is the compliance team's call. Book them for both questions while you are on the call.
